faq.q: Can I control the order of pages and rotate images?
faq.a: Yes. After adding images, each thumbnail can be dragged to reorder, moved up/down with arrows, rotated 90° at a time (shown with a rotation badge), or removed. The PDF is built in the on-screen order. There's also a 'Copy page order' button that lists the files with sizes and rotations so you can confirm the sequence before converting.

faq.q: What page sizes and fit modes are available?
faq.a: Page sizes are A4, US Letter, Legal, A5, 'Fit to Image', or custom dimensions in mm. Orientation can be Auto (per image), Portrait or Landscape, with margins of none/5/10/20 mm. Fit modes are 'Fit inside' (whole image kept, may leave margins), 'Fill/Cover' (fills the page, may crop) and 'Stretch'. For document scans, Fit avoids cropping the edge of a certificate.

faq.q: How do I keep the PDF file size down?
faq.a: Keep 'Re-encode images as JPEG' ticked and lower the JPEG Quality slider (default 85%) — there's a live estimated size. Presets help too: 'Smallest file' uses 60% quality with small margins, while 'Photo album' keeps 95% quality. Note a PDF of images is roughly the sum of those images, so resizing or compressing photos before converting has the biggest effect.

faq.q: Will the text in my scanned pages be searchable?
faq.a: No. The PDF contains pictures of your pages, not text — it isn't searchable, selectable or readable by a screen reader. If you need searchable content, the images have to go through OCR separately first. Everything runs in your browser via pdf-lib, so nothing is uploaded, and you can add page numbers at the bottom if needed.
